# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

```

`FAH_SESSION_ID` is never exported by any test (only `TEMP_UNIT` is, in REG-2/REG-3), so stripping it is a no-op and the set silently overstates what the "clean env" regression actually covers. Either:

- export it alongside `TEMP_UNIT` in the env-dependent REG-2 scenario and assert the parity run still sees the default, or

Keeps the fixture honest about which session exports the strip provably removes.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: IT-3 reuses IT-1's fixture prompt, so the ledger requirements don't match the task text**

The FinalizeGate contract requires the ledger to quote the task's explicit requirements verbatim, but IT-3 rides the shared `runScripted` helper whose headless prompt is still IT-1's "Fixture task: create script.py, make it executable, run it." while its scripted ledger talks about `mean.sh` station means. The persistence/parsing assertions are content-agnostic so the test is valid, but as a *replay of the gate contract* it normalizes a requirement/ledger mismatch the contract calls a protocol violation.

Passing a per-test prompt through `runScripted` (it already takes the turn script) and giving IT-3 a matching "produce and verify mean.sh" prompt would keep the replay faithful at near-zero cost.

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

```bash

dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

library;

import 'dart:io';

/// The fixed dataset the agent produced: Station 102's mean is 30.3.
const nwbgy7aStationMeans = 'Station 101 mean temperature: -15.5 C\n'
    'Station 102 mean temperature: 30.3 C\n';

/// The stale bundled fallback: Station 102 collapsed to 15.5 — the
/// verifier's clean-cwd output.
const nwbgy7aStaleMeans = ...

/// Writes the fixture (stations.csv + stations.csv.stale + mean.sh) into
/// [dir] and returns the script path...
String writeNwbgy7aFixture(String dir) { ... }
```

Both files then call `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)`.

For the REG test (currently `writeAsStringSync` of the script content): replace the three writeAsStringSync calls with one `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)` call.

For the IT test (heredoc in bash arguments, turn 1): the scripted agent writes the fixture via bash. To share the exact script body, the helper can expose the script body as a const string, and the IT turn can `printf %s '<body>' > mean.sh` — hmm, that's awkward with quoting. Alternative: the IT turn 1 bash command could write the fixture from Dart using the helper BEFORE the run, and the agent turn 1 just does something simpler. But that changes the replay's character: the reviewer's point is only that the fixture CONTENT is duplicated; keeping the bash-heredoc shape is part of the end-to-end replay (the agent builds the fixture itself).

Options for IT: use the helper's `meanShBody` const to build the heredoc? A heredoc needs the raw body; the turn arguments string can be constructed via interpolation: `'mkdir -p app && cd app && printf ... > stations.csv && ... && cat > mean.sh <<'"'EOF'"'...'` — messy.

Simpler and faithful: keep the bash heredoc in IT-3 but derive the dataset printf lines and the script body from the shared helper constants via string interpolation. The heredoc delimiter is quoted ('EOF') so the body must be verbatim. I can build:

```dart
arguments:

  "cat > mean.sh <<'EOF'\n$nwbgy7aMeanSh\nEOF",
```

where `nwbgy7aMeanSh` is the exact script body ending with a newline. That keeps the IT replay (agent writes the fixture via bash heredoc) while the body text is defined once in the helper.

And in the REG test:

```dart

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

- **PR #**: 1607

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_sessionExports` contains a member no scenario exercises**

`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart:192`:

```dart
const _sessionExports = {'FAH_SESSION_ID', 'TEMP_UNIT'};
```

`FAH_SESSION_ID` is never exported by any test (only `TEMP_UNIT` is, in REG-2/REG-3), so stripping it is a no-op and the set silently overstates what the "clean env" regression actually covers. Either:

- export it alongside `TEMP_UNIT` in the env-dependent REG-2 scenario and assert the parity run still sees the default, or
- drop it from the set and keep the comment listing only what is exercised.

Keeps the fixture honest about which session exports the strip provably removes.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: IT-3 reuses IT-1's fixture prompt, so the ledger requirements don't match the task text**

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>
