# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1607
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1607
- **Title**: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1605` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +320
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:18:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:31:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

-    '## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

# pr-1607: gh-1605 FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

Closes #1605
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

library;

import 'dart:io';

/// The fixed dataset the agent produced: Station 102's mean is 30.3.
const nwbgy7aStationMeans = 'Station 101 mean temperature: -15.5 C\n'
    'Station 102 mean temperature: 30.3 C\n';

/// The stale bundled fallback: Station 102 collapsed to 15.5 — the
/// verifier's clean-cwd output.
const nwbgy7aStaleMeans = ...

/// Writes the fixture (stations.csv + stations.csv.stale + mean.sh) into
/// [dir] and returns the script path...
String writeNwbgy7aFixture(String dir) { ... }
```

Both files then call `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)`.

For the REG test (currently `writeAsStringSync` of the script content): replace the three writeAsStringSync calls with one `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)` call.

For the IT test (heredoc in bash arguments, turn 1): the scripted agent writes the fixture via bash. To share the exact script body, the helper can expose the script body as a const string, and the IT turn can `printf %s '<body>' > mean.sh` — hmm, that's awkward with quoting. Alternative: the IT turn 1 bash command could write the fixture from Dart using the helper BEFORE the run, and the agent turn 1 just does something simpler. But that changes the replay's character: the reviewer's point is only that the fixture CONTENT is duplicated; keeping the bash-heredoc shape is part of the end-to-end replay (the agent builds the fixture itself).

Options for IT: use the helper's `meanShBody` const to build the heredoc? A heredoc needs the raw body; the turn arguments string can be constructed via interpolation: `'mkdir -p app && cd app && printf ... > stations.csv && ... && cat > mean.sh <<'"'EOF'"'...'` — messy.

Simpler and faithful: keep the bash heredoc in IT-3 but derive the dataset printf lines and the script body from the shared helper constants via string interpolation. The heredoc delimiter is quoted ('EOF') so the body must be verbatim. I can build:

```dart
arguments:

  "cat > mean.sh <<'EOF'\n$nwbgy7aMeanSh\nEOF",
```

where `nwbgy7aMeanSh` is the exact script body ending with a newline. That keeps the IT replay (agent writes the fixture via bash heredoc) while the body text is defined once in the helper.

And in the REG test:

```dart

Both files then call `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)`.

For the REG test (currently `writeAsStringSync` of the script content): replace the three writeAsStringSync calls with one `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)` call.

For the IT test (heredoc in bash arguments, turn 1): the scripted agent writes the fixture via bash. To share the exact script body, the helper can expose the script body as a const string, and the IT turn can `printf %s '<body>' > mean.sh` — hmm, that's awkward with quoting. Alternative: the IT turn 1 bash command could write the fixture from Dart using the helper BEFORE the run, and the agent turn 1 just does something simpler. But that changes the replay's character: the reviewer's point is only that the fixture CONTENT is duplicated; keeping the bash-heredoc shape is part of the end-to-end replay (the agent builds the fixture itself).

Alternative: the IT turn 1 bash command could write the fixture from Dart using the helper BEFORE the run, and the agent turn 1 just does something simpler. But that changes the replay's character: the reviewer's point is only that the fixture CONTENT is duplicated; keeping the bash-heredoc shape is part of the end-to-end replay (the agent builds the fixture itself).

Both files then call `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)`.

For the REG test (currently `writeAsStringSync` of the script content): replace the three writeAsStringSync calls with one `writeNwbgy7aFixture(appDir)` call.

For the IT test (heredoc in bash arguments, turn 1): the scripted agent writes the fixture via bash. To share the exact script body, the helper can expose the script body as a const string, and the IT turn can `printf %s '<body>' > mean.sh` — hmm, that's awkward with quoting. Alternative: the IT turn 1 bash command could write the fixture from Dart using the helper BEFORE the run, and the agent turn 1 just does something simpler. But that changes the replay's character: the reviewer's point is only that the fixture CONTENT is duplicated; keeping the bash-heredoc shape is part of the end-to-end replay (the agent builds the fixture itself).

Options for IT: use the helper's `meanShBody` const to build the heredoc? A heredoc needs the raw body; the turn arguments string can be constructed via interpolation: `'mkdir -p app && cd app && printf ... > stations.csv && ... && cat > mean.sh <<'"'EOF'"'...'` — messy.

Simpler and faithful: keep the bash heredoc in IT-3 but derive the dataset printf lines and the script body from the shared helper constants via string interpolation. The heredoc delimiter is quoted ('EOF') so the body must be verbatim. I can build:

```dart

  "printf 'station,temp\\n101,-15.5\\n102,15.5\\n' > stations.csv.stale && "
  "cat > mean.sh <<'EOF'\n$nwbgy7aMeanSh\nEOF",
```

where `nwbgy7aMeanSh` is the exact script body ending with a newline. That keeps the IT replay (agent writes the fixture via bash heredoc) while the body text is defined once in the helper.

And in the REG test:

```dart

```

One subtlety: in the REG test the heredoc-escaped version currently uses `\$(dirname "\$0")` etc. In a shared const (non-raw, triple-quoted Dart string) I need proper Dart escaping:

```dart
const nwbgy7aMeanSh = '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n'
    ...
```

Let me write it as a final raw-ish string. The body:

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -f stations.csv ]]; then
  data=stations.csv
else
  data="$(dirname "$0")/stations.csv.stale"
fi
awk -F, 'NR > 1 { sum[$1] += $2; n[$1]++ }
  END { for (s in sum) printf "Station %s mean temperature: %.1f C\n", s, sum[s]/n[s] }' "$data" | sort
```

In Dart, I can use a raw triple-quoted string r'''...''' — then `$1`, `$0`, `${...}`, `\n` stay literal. The awk printf contains `\n` which must be literal backslash-n in the script — raw string handles that. But careful: the body must NOT contain `'''`. It doesn't.

So:

```dart
const nwbgy7aMeanSh = r'''
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -f stations.csv ]]; then
  data=stations.csv
else
  data="$(dirname "$0")/stations.csv.stale"
fi
awk -F, 'NR > 1 { sum[$1] += $2; n[$1]++ }
  END { for (s in sum) printf "Station %s mean temperature: %.1f C\n", s, sum[s]/n[s] }' "$data" | sort
''';
```

Note: raw triple-quoted string starting right after `r'''` with a newline means the string begins with `\n`. For heredoc usage in IT: `cat > mean.sh <<'EOF'\n$nwbgy7aMeanSh\nEOF` — with the leading newline in the const, we'd get `<<'EOF'` then newline then the body (which itself starts with newline → an empty first line — bad!). Hmm.

Let me define the const WITHOUT leading newline: use a raw string but strip. Options: define with explicit line splicing:

```dart
const nwbgy7aMeanSh = r'''#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
...
awk ... | sort
''';
```

Put `#!/usr/bin/env bash` immediately after `r'''`. That gives a body that starts with the shebang and ends with `\n` after `sort`. 

Then in the REG helper: `File('$dir/mean.sh').writeAsStringSync(nwbgy7aMeanSh)`.

In IT: 
```dart
arguments: 'mkdir -p app && cd app && '
    "printf 'station,temp\\n101,-15.5\\n102,30.3\\n' > stations.csv && "
    "printf 'station,temp\\n101,-15.5\\n102,15.5\\n' > stations.csv.stale && "
    "cat > mean.sh <<'FA_EOF'\n$nwbgy7aMeanSh\nFA_EOF",
```

Wait — heredoc via `bash -c 'cat > mean.sh <<'EOF'\n...\nEOF'`: how does the harness run bash arguments? It runs `bash -c <command>` presumably. Multi-line command strings should work. The current IT code already embeds a multi-line heredoc in the arguments (the existing test passes), with `r"""..."""` raw string containing actual newlines. So I keep the same shape: `... > stations.csv.stale && ` + `cat > mean.sh <<'EOF'\n<body>\nEOF`. With body ending in `\n` already, we get `...sort\nEOF` — a blank line before EOF. Heredoc terminator: the terminator must be alone on its line; a blank line before it is fine (it's part of content). Actually wait: body ends with `| sort\n`. content.thinking:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

+  /// The grader-parity re-run: a fresh subprocess from a NEUTRAL cwd
+  /// (never the session cwd) with the session exports stripped from the
+  /// session environment — the invocation shape the verifier uses. Takes
+  /// the same [sessionExports] the in-session run merged in, so the
+  /// strip is provably exercised for every member of [_sessionExports].
+  Future<ProcessResult> graderParityRun(
+    String script, {
+    Map<String, String> sessionExports = const {},
+  }) => Process.run(
+    '/bin/bash',
+    [script],
+    workingDirectory: '/',
+    environment: {
+      for (final entry in {
+        ...Platform.environment,
+        ...sessionExports,
+      }.entries)
+        if (!_sessionExports.contains(entry.key)) entry.key: entry.value,
+    },
+  );

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.
