blocks.text:
# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"# Thread 1 — `_sessionExports` contains a member no scenario exercises

Fixed — and the suggestion surfaced a real hole deeper than the fixture honesty it asked for.

**What changed** (`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart`):

- REG-2 now exports **both** members of `_sessionExports` in its in-session run — `TEMP_UNIT: F` and `FAH_SESSION_ID: sess-42` — and the script echoes both (`unit: ${TEMP_UNIT:-C}`, `session: ${FAH_SESSION_ID:-none}`), asserting the parity run sees only the defaults (`unit: C`, `session: none`).
- `graderParityRun` takes the same `sessionExports` the in-session run merged in, so the strip operates on a session environment that provably carries both variables — not on a base that never had them.

**The bonus find:** making the strip assertable exposed that it was never real. `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so every key absent from the provided env map is re-inherited from the test process — and the runner's own environment carries a live `FAH_SESSION_ID`. The parity child saw `session: 01a13b0f-…` on the first run of the strengthened test. The fix passes `includeParentEnvironment: false`, so the child env is exactly the session env minus the session exports. With the old code, dropping `FAH_SESSION_ID` from `_sessionExports` (or any future export) would have leaked silently; now REG-2 fails on it.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).

{"content":"# Thread 1 — `_sessionExports` contains a member no scenario exercises

Fixed — and the suggestion surfaced a real hole deeper than the fixture honesty it asked for.

**What changed** (`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart`):

- REG-2 now exports **both** members of `_sessionExports` in its in-session run — `TEMP_UNIT: F` and `FAH_SESSION_ID: sess-42` — and the script echoes both (`unit: ${TEMP_UNIT:-C}`, `session: ${FAH_SESSION_ID:-none}`), asserting the parity run sees only the defaults (`unit: C`, `session: none`).
- `graderParityRun` takes the same `sessionExports` the in-session run merged in, so the strip operates on a session environment that provably carries both variables — not on a base that never had them.

**The bonus find:** making the strip assertable exposed that it was never real. `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so every key absent from the provided env map is re-inherited from the test process — and the runner's own environment carries a live `FAH_SESSION_ID`. The parity child saw `session: 01a13b0f-…` on the first run of the strengthened test. The fix passes `includeParentEnvironment: false`, so the child env is exactly the session env minus the session exports. With the old code, dropping `FAH_SESSION_ID` from `_sessionExports` (or any future export) would have leaked silently; now REG-2 fails on it.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

blocks.text:
# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"# Thread 1 — `_sessionExports` contains a member no scenario exercises

Fixed — and the suggestion surfaced a real hole deeper than the fixture honesty it asked for.

**What changed** (`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart`):

- REG-2 now exports **both** members of `_sessionExports` in its in-session run — `TEMP_UNIT: F` and `FAH_SESSION_ID: sess-42` — and the script echoes both (`unit: ${TEMP_UNIT:-C}`, `session: ${FAH_SESSION_ID:-none}`), asserting the parity run sees only the defaults (`unit: C`, `session: none`).
- `graderParityRun` takes the same `sessionExports` the in-session run merged in, so the strip operates on a session environment that provably carries both variables — not on a base that never had them.

**The bonus find:** making the strip assertable exposed that it was never real. `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so every key absent from the provided env map is re-inherited from the test process — and the runner's own environment carries a live `FAH_SESSION_ID`. The parity child saw `session: 01a13b0f-…` on the first run of the strengthened test. The fix passes `includeParentEnvironment: false`, so the child env is exactly the session env minus the session exports. With the old code, dropping `FAH_SESSION_ID` from `_sessionExports` (or any future export) would have leaked silently; now REG-2 fails on it.

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).

# Rework: gh-1605 FinalizeGate grader parity — thread fixes + merge conflict

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflict** with `main` in `CHANGELOG.md` — resolved by keeping both `## Unreleased` entries (this branch's gh-1605 entry and main's gh-1603 entry), newest-first, matching the file's convention. `git diff --check` clean, no conflict markers remain.
- **Review thread 1** (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sYmlk`) — `_sessionExports` listed `FAH_SESSION_ID`, which no scenario exercised. Fixed by exercising it — and the fix surfaced a real bug: `Process.run`'s default `includeParentEnvironment: true` re-inherits stripped keys from the runner env, which genuinely carries a live `FAH_SESSION_ID`. The strengthened REG-2 caught its own fixture leaking `session: 01a13b0f-…` into the parity run on first execution. The parity subprocess now runs with `includeParentEnvironment: false`, so "clean env" is real and the strip is regression-armed.
- **Review thread 2** (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sYmtX`) — IT-3 rode IT-1's fixture prompt while its ledger talked `mean.sh`, a requirement/ledger mismatch the gate contract itself calls a violation. `runScripted` now takes a per-test `prompt`; IT-3 passes a matching "create mean.sh … verify the output" task text and its ledger quotes the requirement verbatim (asserted).
- **Review thread 3** (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sYmzG`) — the nwbgy7a evidence fixture (stations.csv + stale fallback + awk aggregation) was built twice (Dart `writeAsStringSync` in REG-1, bash heredoc in IT-3). Extracted to `test/support/nwbgy7a_fixture.dart` (the repo's shared-test-support location); the IT producer command is derived from the same consts as the REG writer, so the two layers cannot drift.
- The three `threadId: null` records in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (review summary, review-verdict record, rework-consume notice) are machine notices — the verdict/consume records are marked "do not reply"; no reply entries were fabricated for them.

## Approach

Surgical, thread-by-thread, TDD where it bites:

1. Resolved the `CHANGELOG.md` conflict; staged; verified with `git diff --check`.
2. Thread 1: gave REG-2 both exports and had the parity run strip from the same merged session env. RED came free: the first run of the strengthened assertions failed (`session: 01a13b0f-…` instead of `session: none`), exposing the `includeParentEnvironment` inheritance hole. GREEN: `includeParentEnvironment: false` on the parity `Process.run`.
3. Thread 2: added the `prompt` parameter (default preserves IT-1/IT-2 behavior), gave IT-3 its own task text, made the ledger quote it verbatim, added a verbatim-quote assertion mirroring IT-1's.
4. Thread 3: single-source fixture helper; REG writes it from Dart, IT produces it via a command derived from the same consts.
5. Full verification (below) run only after all edits were frozen.

## Files Modified

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:

blocks.text:
# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

**What changed** (`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart`):

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

{"content":"# Thread 1 — `_sessionExports` contains a member no scenario exercises

Fixed — and the suggestion surfaced a real hole deeper than the fixture honesty it asked for.

**What changed** (`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart`):

- REG-2 now exports **both** members of `_sessionExports` in its in-session run — `TEMP_UNIT: F` and `FAH_SESSION_ID: sess-42` — and the script echoes both (`unit: ${TEMP_UNIT:-C}`, `session: ${FAH_SESSION_ID:-none}`), asserting the parity run sees only the defaults (`unit: C`, `session: none`).
- `graderParityRun` takes the same `sessionExports` the in-session run merged in, so the strip operates on a session environment that provably carries both variables — not on a base that never had them.

**The bonus find:** making the strip assertable exposed that it was never real. `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so every key absent from the provided env map is re-inherited from the test process — and the runner's own environment carries a live `FAH_SESSION_ID`. The parity child saw `session: 01a13b0f-…` on the first run of the strengthened test. The fix passes `includeParentEnvironment: false`, so the child env is exactly the session env minus the session exports. With the old code, dropping `FAH_SESSION_ID` from `_sessionExports` (or any future export) would have leaked silently; now REG-2 fails on it.

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1605 FinalizeGate grader parity — thread fixes + merge conflict

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflict** with `main` in `CHANGELOG.md` — resolved by keeping both `## Unreleased` entries (this branch's gh-1605 entry and main's gh-1603 entry), newest-first, matching the file's convention. `git diff --check` clean, no conflict markers remain.
- **Review thread 1** (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sYmlk`) — `_sessionExports` listed `FAH_SESSION_ID`, which no scenario exercised. Fixed by exercising it — and the fix surfaced a real bug: `Process.run`'s default `includeParentEnvironment: true` re-inherits stripped keys from the runner env, which genuinely carries a live `FAH_SESSION_ID`. The strengthened REG-2 caught its own fixture leaking `session: 01a13b0f-…` into the parity run on first execution. The parity subprocess now runs with `includeParentEnvironment: false`, so "clean env" is real and the strip is regression-armed.
- **Review thread 2** (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sYmtX`) — IT-3 rode IT-1's fixture prompt while its ledger talked `mean.sh`, a requirement/ledger mismatch the gate contract itself calls a violation. `runScripted` now takes a per-test `prompt`; IT-3 passes a matching "create mean.sh … verify the output" task text and its ledger quotes the requirement verbatim (asserted).
- **Review thread 3** (`PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sYmzG`) — the nwbgy7a evidence fixture (stations.csv + stale fallback + awk aggregation) was built twice (Dart `writeAsStringSync` in REG-1, bash heredoc in IT-3). Extracted to `test/support/nwbgy7a_fixture.dart` (the repo's shared-test-support location); the IT producer command is derived from the same consts as the REG writer, so the two layers cannot drift.
- The three `threadId: null` records in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (review summary, review-verdict record, rework-consume notice) are machine notices — the verdict/consume records are marked "do not reply"; no reply entries were fabricated for them.

## Approach

Surgical, thread-by-thread, TDD where it bites:

1. Resolved the `CHANGELOG.md` conflict; staged; verified with `git diff --check`.
2. Thread 1: gave REG-2 both exports and had the parity run strip from the same merged session env. RED came free: the first run of the strengthened assertions failed (`session: 01a13b0f-…` instead of `session: none`), exposing the `includeParentEnvironment` inheritance hole. GREEN: `includeParentEnvironment: false` on the parity `Process.run`.
3. Thread 2: added the `prompt` parameter (default preserves IT-1/IT-2 behavior), gave IT-3 its own task text, made the ledger quote it verbatim, added a verbatim-quote assertion mirroring IT-1's.
4. Thread 3: single-source fixture helper; REG writes it from Dart, IT produces it via a command derived from the same consts.
5. Full verification (below) run only after all edits were frozen.

## Files Modified

- `CHANGELOG.md` — merge-conflict resolution (both gh-1605 and gh-1603 entries kept).
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` — REG-2 exports both session vars and asserts the clean-env defaults; `graderParityRun` takes `sessionExports` and runs with `includeParentEnvironment: false`; REG-1 uses the shared fixture; cross-references to the IT copy.
- `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — `runScripted(..., {String prompt})`; IT-3 uses `_parityTaskPrompt` + verbatim-quote assertion; IT-3 turn 1 builds the fixture via the shared `nwbgy7aProduceCommand()`.
- `test/support/nwbgy7a_fixture.dart` — **new** shared nwbgy7a evidence fixture (dataset consts, `mean.sh` body, `writeNwbgy7aFixture`, `nwbgy7aProduceCommand`).

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

**What changed** (`test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart`):

messages.preview: Found the root cause — a real hole the suggestion was pointing at: `Process.run` defaults to `includeParentEnvironment: true`, so stripped keys get re-inherited from the runner's env (which genuinely …

blocks.text:
The code looks correct: `{...Platform.environment, ...sessionExports}` then strip `_sessionExports` members. So why did `FAH_SESSION_ID` survive into the child env?

OH WAIT. I see it — `Process.run(environment: ...)` in Dart: when you pass `environment`, does it REPLACE the whole env or MERGE with the parent's? It REPLACES (`includeParentEnvironment` defaults to **true**!). `Process.run` has `includeParentEnvironment = true` by default, meaning the parent's environment is INCLUDED (merged) with the provided map — overriding nothing... actually: if `includeParentEnvironment` is true, the child gets parent env + provided map (provided wins on conflicts). So even though my map strips FAH_SESSION_ID, the parent's real FAH_SESSION_ID is re-added by `includeParentEnvironment: true`!

That also explains why the ORIGINAL code (stripping from Platform.environment only) "worked" for TEMP_UNIT — TEMP_UNIT isn't in the parent env, and there `includeParentEnvironment` re-adds everything from parent minus nothing relevant... wait for TEMP_UNIT: parent env has no TEMP_UNIT, provided env = parent minus exports (TEMP_UNIT not in parent anyway) → child sees no TEMP_UNIT → default C. It worked by luck: the parent env didn't contain the stripped variable.

The REAL harness (the fa agent) presumably launches the verifier subprocess with a genuinely clean env — the prompt's "clean env (no session-exported vars)" is the contract. For the test to PROVE the strip, it must set `includeParentEnvironment: false`... but then Platform.environment wouldn't be included at all — the child would get ONLY the stripped map. That's the truly faithful "clean env" simulation: the grader runs the script with its own neutral environment, not inheriting the session's.

Hmm, but the original test's intent: "clean env (no session-exported vars)" — the grader's subprocess env = the session env minus session exports? Or a fully neutral env? The FinalizeGate prompt says "clean env (no session-exported vars)". The nwbgy7a verifier used `subprocess.run` with a fresh environment (env=None would inherit the HARNESS's env, not the agent session's).

The cleanest faithful simulation that PROVES the strip: build the session env (Platform.environment + exports), strip the exports, and pass with `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Then:
- TEMP_UNIT: absent from stripped map → child sees nothing → default C. Proves TEMP_UNIT strip.
- FAH_SESSION_ID: present (sess-42 from exports, or the harness's real UUID from Platform.environment) → stripped → child sees nothing → default none. Proves FAH_SESSION_ID strip — and interestingly, even without my sessionExports param, the harness's REAL FAH_SESSION_ID in the runner env makes the strip observable with includeParentEnvironment: false. That's a genuinely real regression: if someone removed FAH_SESSION_ID from _sessionExports, the child would see the harness session id — exactly the leak the gate forbids.

So: `graderParityRun` should use `includeParentEnvironment: false`. Is that faithful to what the verifier does? `subprocess.run([...], env=None)` inherits the PYTHON process env (the verifier harness env), which contains no agent-session exports. `includeParentEnvironment: false` + a map built from session-env-minus-exports ≈ "the verifier's env has none of the session's exports". With includeParentEnvironment: false, env vars like PATH would be missing → bash might fail (`/bin/bash` absolute path is fine; `dirname`, `awk`, `printf`, `sort` are absolute-ish? `awk`/`sort`/`dirname` are resolved via PATH — with empty PATH, bash uses a default PATH usually (bash sets a default PATH if unset... actually bash provides a default PATH only if PATH is unset entirely; here PATH would be absent → confstr _CS_PATH default: /bin:/usr/bin — bash does fall back to that). Risky.

Safer: keep includeParentEnvironment default (true) BUT the strip then must be enforced differently... With includeParentEnvironment: true and env map provided, provided keys override parent keys, but keys ABSENT from the provided map are inherited from parent. There's no way to REMOVE a parent var with includeParentEnvironment: true.

Alternative approach — keep the strip against the merged session env but ALSO assert at the Dart level that the parity env map doesn't contain the exports... but the actual child env is what matters.

Better: pass `includeParentEnvironment: false` and provide the full stripped map (which retains PATH etc. since Platform.environment minus exports keeps PATH). That's precise: child env = session env minus exports, verbatim. PATH survives (it's not a session export). TEMP_UNIT survives if the runner has it... wait — if the RUNNER's env has TEMP_UNIT set (it doesn't), the in-session test merges 'F' anyway. Fine.

So the fix: add `includeParentEnvironment: false` to `graderParityRun`'s Process.run. Then:
- REG-2 child env = Platform.environment + exports, minus FAH_SESSION_ID & TEMP_UNIT → `unit: C`, `session: none`. Both strips proven. And FAH_SESSION_ID strip is proven against the harness's REAL session id in Platform.environment — a genuinely exercised strip.

This is exactly the kind of bug the suggestion thread was pointing at — the "clean env" regression wasn't actually clean. The reviewer said "the set silently overstates what the regression covers" — and indeed the test was structurally unable to catch a leak. My change makes it airtight.

Also note: this discovery means the ORIGINAL PR's parity test had a latent hole: `graderParityRun` with includeParentEnvironment:true never strips anything the parent env carries. Fixing it now.

Similarly REG-3 (no false positive): its parity run gets the same treatment; script reads no env, fine.

# weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
